question: Does matching initial grid-state hash capacity to sparse series reduce native CPU and memory without dense-query regressions?
baseline: R29 LLVM 22.1.8 O2 jemalloc stock binary, sha256 5d629ddfda91919402fdf8475ec3da9fe718d48ef386bc51be677264df6dc9ef
candidate: Only TimeSeriesBucketsHashTableGrower: initial degree 4 -> 1, reserve starts at 1, maxFill becomes bufSize()/2 + bufSize()/4. No R32 finalizer or other lab patch.
fixture: Exact same stored TimeSeries snapshot and generated native PromQL for stock and candidate. Sparse high-cardinality and dense multi-bucket negative controls. Publish generator, query, physical hashes and binary identities.
single_variable: Initial bucket-map capacity, with corrected 3/4 fill arithmetic for two-cell maps
math_bound: Singleton main-buffer bytes 16*C -> 2*C, where C=sizeof(cell); saves 14*C per live state. Key zero is stored separately, and end-to-end savings must be measured. At capacity>=4, fill threshold is unchanged.
falsifier: Any oracle difference, malformed-state acceptance regression, absent-key loop, dense regression beyond drift, OOM, source/flags mismatch, or no useful total CPU/RSS benefit
test_matrix: zero/nonzero key; one/many populated buckets; empty/single/overlapping grids; merge/state roundtrip; NaN/Inf and duplicate samples; native sparse stage/project/whole plus dense negative controls; fresh-server ABBA
runner_budget: One incremental O2 build with existing ccache, then local 4-vCPU/4-GiB benchmark. No duplicate builds or cancellation.
